identity.title: Lack of other molecules in CO-rich debris discs: is it primordial or secondary gas?
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present millimetre molecular line observations of nine circumstellar discs around A-type stars: four CO-rich debris discs (HD 21997, HD 121617, HD 131488, HD 131835) and five old Herbig Ae protoplanetary discs (HD 139614, HD 141569, HD 142666, HD 145718, HD 100453).
Observations of our targets were performed with the ALMA 12m Array during 2018 and 2019 in the framework of two projects (2017.1.01545.S and 2018.1.01429.S, PI: Th. Henning).

question.value: Whether the gas in CO-rich debris discs is a remnant from the earlier Class II phase (hybrid scenario) or of secondary origin driven by icy planetesimal destruction, tested via millimeter observations of simple molecules.

evidence.quote: The nature of the gas in CO-rich debris discs remains poorly understood, as it could either be a remnant from the earlier Class II phase or of secondary origin, driven by the destruction of icy planetesimals.
The aim of this paper was to elucidate the origin of the gas content in the debris discs via various simple molecules that are often detected in the less-evolved Class II discs.
Observations of our targets were performed with the ALMA 12m Array during 2018 and 2019 in the framework of two projects (2017.1.01545.S and 2018.1.01429.S, PI: Th. Henning).

analysis_steps.goal: Measure integrated line fluxes and 3-sigma upper limits from moment-0 maps

method.value: Construct zeroth-moment maps over line velocity ranges, measure fluxes using fitted elliptical apertures, estimate uncertainties from 16 random background apertures, and derive 3-sigma upper limits for non-detections using HCN or IMSMOOTH-smoothed archival 12CO cubes as templates.

evidence.quote: In the detected cases, zeroth moment maps were constructed by integrating over the velocity ranges of the significant line emission.

The integrated line fluxes were derived by using elliptical apertures that were fitted to the observed velocity-integrated emission. To estimate flux uncertainties, we randomly distributed 16 identical elliptical apertures in the background region and computed the standard deviation of the fluxes obtained in them.
The CO measurements were taken from the ALMA archive and the template data cubes were smoothed using the IMSMOOTH CASA task to obtain the same synthesised beam as that of the given line.

key_parameters.value: 16 random background apertures for uncertainty; 3-sigma upper limits

evidence.quote: To estimate flux uncertainties, we randomly distributed 16 identical elliptical apertures in the background region and computed the standard deviation of the fluxes obtained in them.

analysis_steps.goal: Calculate molecular photodissociation lifetimes under H2 and C shielding

method.value: Compute photodissociation rates k = k0 * theta and lifetimes tau = 1/k as a function of H2 or neutral atomic carbon column density using literature unattenuated rates and shielding functions.

evidence.quote: The photodissociation rate of a given molecule can be estimated as $k = k_0 \theta$, where $k_0$ is the unattenuated photodissociation rate of the molecule, while $\theta$ is the shielding function (cite: heays2017).
Figure [3](#fig:pdlifetimes) shows the photodissociation lifetimes ($\tau = 1/k$) of the targeted molecules and CO for the various H$_2$ or neutral atomic carbon column densities.

assumptions.value: Only the interstellar UV radiation field is taken into account; dust attenuation is negligible in debris discs

evidence.quote: We took into account only the interstellar UV radiation field in our calculations.

analysis_steps.goal: Simulate time-dependent chemical evolution and non-LTE line radiative transfer

method.value: Run the single-point ALCHEMIC chemical kinetics code over a 2D temperature-density grid for 1 Myr across five sets of initial abundances (varying H2/He depletion), then compute non-LTE line brightness temperatures and flux ratios with RADEX.

evidence.quote: To reproduce detections of the CO isotopologues and non-detections of HCO$^+$, CN, HCN, C$_{2}$H, and CS in debris discs, we have utilised the ALCHEMIC chemical model (cite: Semenov_ea_2010) and the RADEX line radiative transfer code (cite: radex), and adopted a temperature-density grid.
Using the above chemical model, we have calculated the abundance evolution over 1 Myr for constant physical conditions.
We have calculated the line brightness temperatures with the non-LTE RADEX code.

key_parameters.value: Temperature grid: 10 to 300 K; density grid: 10^3 to 10^7 cm^-3; evolution time: 1 Myr; radial UV optical depth tau = 0 to 1; cosmic ray ionisation rate: 1.3e-17 s^-1; H2 depletion factors: 1, 2, 5, 10, 100

evidence.quote: We have modelled chemical evolution over a temperature range between 10 and 300 K and densities between $10^3$ and $10^7$ cm$^{-3}$ (or between $\approx 4 \times 10^{-21}$ and $4 \times 10^{-17}$ g cm$^{-3}$).
The ionisation rate was set to $1.3 \times 10^{-17}$ s$^{-1}$, corresponding to a galactic cosmic ray ionisation rate.
In the other four sets, we multiplied the relative abundances of all species other than hydrogen and helium by a factor of 2, 5, 10, and 100, respectively.

key_parameters.value: Emitting gas column length = 15 au; line FWHM = 1 km s^-1

evidence.quote: We have calculated the line brightness temperatures assuming the length of the emitting gas column of 15 au and a line full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 1 km s$^{-1}$.

assumptions.value: Dust-to-gas mass ratio set to 10^-10 for 0.1 um grains; unattenuated UV field equal to vertical ISRF; stellar X-rays and high-energy particles neglected; fixed isotopic ratios 12C/13C = 77 and 16O/18O = 560

evidence.quote: Since primordial (sub-)micron-sized dust has already evolved and became severely depleted, we decided to set the corresponding dust-to-gas mass ratio to a value of $10^{-10}$ for $0.1$ $\mu$m-sized grains, effectively turning off dust-surface reactions.

Since $^{13}$C and $^{18}$O are not included in the chemical network, we have used fixed isotopic ratios C$^{12}$/C$^{13} = 77$ and O$^{16}$/O$^{18} = 560$ to scale down the resulting molecular abundances (cite: wilson_rood_1994_isotope_ratio).

validation.value: 1 Myr evolution timespan verified to reach chemical equilibrium within 1-100 kyr for simple molecules

evidence.quote: This timespan was long enough to reach a chemical equilibrium within 1-100 kyr for the observed, chemically simple molecules (depending on density).

evidence.loc: Effect of hydrogen depletion on disc scale height
evidence.quote: First, all available carbon is assumed to be locked in CO molecules. Then, the remaining oxygen and available hydrogen are assumed to form water molecules. After that, the remaining hydrogen (if any) is assumed to be bound in H$_2$ molecules. As water can be rapidly photodissociated in the optically thin debris disc, we consider two extreme cases – with and without water formation.

findings_qualitative.value: CN, HCN, HCO+, and CS lines are detected in all four old Herbig Ae protoplanetary discs (HD 100453, HD 139614, HD 142666, HD 145718), and C2H is detected in HD 139614 and HD 142666.

evidence.quote: By inspecting the obtained data cubes, we found significant CN, HCN, and HCO$^+$ emission towards all four targeted HAe protoplanetary discs (HD 100453, HD 139614, HD 142666, and HD 145718), while the C$_{2}$H line was detected only in HD 139614 and HD 142666 (Figs. [1](#fig:peak), [\[fig:spectra\]](#fig:spectra)).
The J=$5-4$ transition of the CS molecule (Band 6, 244.9355565 GHz) was also detected in one of the additional coarse-resolution spectral windows in all four discs.

findings_qualitative.value: None of the four CO-rich debris discs nor the transitional/hybrid disc HD 141569 exhibit detectable emission in CN, HCN, HCO+, C2H, or CS.

evidence.quote: None of the four CO-rich debris discs, nor the disc around HD 141569 exhibited detectable line emission in any data cubes.

findings_qualitative.value: CN, HCN, C2H, and CS have short photodissociation lifetimes in optically thin debris discs regardless of whether shielding is provided by H2 or neutral C, so their non-detections do not rule out the hybrid scenario.

evidence.quote: Without shielding at these long wavelengths, the latter four molecules have only short photodissociation lifetimes both in hybrid and shielded secondary discs, while in protoplanetary environments they could still be protected from UV by the optically thick dust. The observed low line ratios of these four species to CO in the debris disc sample, therefore, do not necessarily preclude the hybrid scenario (Fig. [2](#fig:ratio)).

findings_qualitative.value: HCO+ is expected to be the second brightest line after CO and its intensity strongly depends on the CO/H2 ratio, falling below the current detection limits everywhere in the modelled parameter space once the H2 depletion factor reaches 5 or higher.

evidence.quote: We find that the HCO$^+$ lines should be the second brightest after the CO lines, and that their intensities strongly depend on the overall CO/H$_2$ ratio of the gas.
However, starting from a higher H$_2$ depletion factor of 5, all the predicted HCO$^+$ J=2-1/$^{13}$CO J=2-1 flux ratios fall below the current detection limit.

claims.hypothesis: CO-rich debris discs share molecular composition with mature Herbig Ae protoplanetary discs if their gas is a remnant from the Class II phase.
claims.experiment: Observed CN, HCN, HCO+, C2H, and CS lines in four CO-rich debris discs, four old Herbig Ae protoplanetary discs, and HD 141569 with ALMA Bands 5 and 6, and compared line-to-CO isotopologue flux ratios.
claims.result: CN, HCN, HCO+, and CS were detected in all four Herbig Ae discs (and C2H in two), whereas none of these molecules were detected in the four debris discs or HD 141569, yielding CN, HCN, and HCO+ to CO ratios at least 4x lower than the lowest Herbig Ae disc (HD 100453).
claims.finding: Molecular abundances or physical conditions of the gas in CO-rich debris discs (and HD 141569) are very different from those in Herbig Ae protoplanetary discs.

evidence.quote: None of the four CO-rich debris discs, nor the disc around HD 141569 exhibited detectable line emission in any data cubes.

This is especially striking for the CN, HCN, and HCO$^+$ lines, even for HD 100453 – that exhibits the lowest line ratios – the obtained ratios are at least 4$\times$ higher than the corresponding average upper limits of the debris disc sample. These results suggest that molecular abundances or physical conditions of the gas in the CO-rich debris discs is very different from those in the protoplanetary discs around Herbig Ae stars.

claims.hypothesis: The non-detection of CN, HCN, C2H, and CS in CO-rich debris discs rules out an H2-rich primordial/hybrid gas origin.
claims.experiment: Calculated photodissociation lifetimes under H2 and C shielding and performed ALCHEMIC chemical kinetics and RADEX radiative transfer simulations across a temperature-density grid with varying H2 depletion factors (1 to 100).
claims.result: CN, HCN, C2H, and CS absorb UV photons longward of 110 nm where neither H2 nor C atoms shield effectively, resulting in simulated line intensities well below current detection limits regardless of H2 abundance.
claims.finding: Low line ratios of CN, HCN, C2H, and CS to CO do not preclude the hybrid H2-rich scenario because optically thin dust cannot protect these molecules from UV photodissociation.

evidence.quote: Without shielding at these long wavelengths, the latter four molecules have only short photodissociation lifetimes both in hybrid and shielded secondary discs, while in protoplanetary environments they could still be protected from UV by the optically thick dust. The observed low line ratios of these four species to CO in the debris disc sample, therefore, do not necessarily preclude the hybrid scenario (Fig. [2](#fig:ratio)).

As it can be clearly seen from Fig. [\[fig:violin\]](#fig:violin), all line intensities other than HCO$^+$ are expected to be below the detection limits, regardless of the initial abundances and position in the temperature-density parameter space.

claims.hypothesis: HCO+ emission is sensitive to the H2 content (CO/H2 ratio) in debris discs and can be used to constrain H2 depletion.
claims.experiment: Simulated HCO+ J=2-1 / 13CO J=2-1 flux ratios with ALCHEMIC and RADEX for ISM-like and H2-depleted (factors of 2, 5, 10, 100) compositions and compared them against observational upper limits.
claims.result: In the ISM-like H2-rich case, HCO+ J=2-1 exceeds the detection limit for T > 20 K and CO density of 3–300 cm^-3; for an H2 depletion factor of 2 it exceeds the limit at T > 40 K and density ~80 cm^-3; for H2 depletion >= 5, all predicted HCO+/13CO ratios fall below the detection limit.
claims.finding: HCO+ is the second brightest expected molecule after CO and its flux strongly depends on H2 depletion via H3+ chemistry, though even in the ISM-like scenario parts of the parameter space remain below current non-detection limits.

evidence.quote: We find that the HCO$^+$ lines should be the second brightest after the CO lines, and that their intensities strongly depend on the overall CO/H$_2$ ratio of the gas. However, even in the ISM-like scenario, the simulated HCO$^+$ emission remains weak as required by our non-detections.
In such discs, the HCO$^+$ J=2-1 line would become detectable if the gas is warmer than 20 K and the CO density is about $3-300$ cm$^{-3}$.
However, starting from a higher H$_2$ depletion factor of 5, all the predicted HCO$^+$ J=2-1/$^{13}$CO J=2-1 flux ratios fall below the current detection limit.

why_this_data.value: Selected the four remaining CO-rich debris discs with M_CO > 0.01 M_earth and CO isotopologue data, plus four nearby older (8-10 Myr) Herbig Ae discs and transitional disc HD 141569 as a reference sample; targeted lower rotational transitions in Bands 5 and 6 due to low gas temperatures and low collisional partner densities.

evidence.quote: Therefore, the remaining four CO-rich debris discs, HD 21997, HD 121617, HD 131488, and HD 131835 were selected as targets of this study.

For comparison with our debris disc sample , therefore we observed the same molecules in four nearby ($<$160 pc), older, less gas-rich primordial discs around Herbig Ae stars, HD100453, HD139614, HD142666, and HD145718.

Considering the typical low gas temperatures (cite: kospal2013; hughes2017) and the possible low density of potential collisional partners in CO-bearing debris discs, which can result in low excitation temperatures, we observed the lower transitions for the selected molecules.

why_this_method.value: Used a single-point chemical model on a temperature-density grid because CO emission in optically thin debris discs forms a relatively narrow ring with tight variations in temperature and UV radiation; turned off dust-surface chemistry by setting dust-to-gas ratio to 10^-10 because sub-micron dust is severely depleted.

evidence.quote: Given that the observed CO emission appears as a relatively narrow ring-like structure in optically thin debris discs, we assume a rather tight variation of temperature and UV radiation strength within the gas emitting area.

Since primordial (sub-)micron-sized dust has already evolved and became severely depleted, we decided to set the corresponding dust-to-gas mass ratio to a value of $10^{-10}$ for $0.1$ $\mu$m-sized grains, effectively turning off dust-surface reactions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Direct measurement of hydrogen depletion via vertical temperature and density structure (hydrostatic scale height) using high-resolution multi-J CO ALMA observations.

evidence.loc: Effect of hydrogen depletion on disc scale height
evidence.quote: An alternative method to estimate hydrogen depletion of a debris disc using ALMA is based on direct measurements of their vertical temperature and density structure (cite: hughes2017; kral2019).

limitations_admitted.value: For HD 21997, ~50% of the channels covering the HCO+ line were flagged during calibration, requiring the upper limit velocity window to be shifted to a non-flagged part of the spectrum.

evidence.quote: In the case of HD 21997, $\sim$50% of the channels covering the HCO$^+$ line were flagged during the calibration process not to be used for scientific analysis. Therefore, this upper limit estimate was obtained by slightly shifting the velocity range to a non-flagged part of the spectrum.

limitations_admitted.value: High-energy particle flux and X-ray radiation from the main-sequence stars were neglected in the chemical model.

evidence.quote: High-energetic particle flux and X-ray radiation from the evolved main-sequence star were neglected, as these are much milder compared to the pre-main-sequence phase.

limitations_admitted.value: Current spatial resolution and sensitivity cannot tightly constrain the CO/H2 ratio or the contribution of an extended tenuous disc atmosphere without follow-up higher-resolution CO or deeper HCO+ observations and full thermo-chemical modelling.

evidence.quote: Follow-up higher-resolution CO or more sensitive HCO$^+$ observations combined with feasible thermo-chemical modelling are required to provide tighter constraints on the CO/H$_2$ ratios in these discs.

referee_caveats_inferred: The chemical and radiative transfer modelling relies on a 0D single-point approximation with a fixed 15 au column length and 1 km/s linewidth under a 1D radial ISRF UV attenuation (tau = 0 to 1), neglecting 2D/3D disc geometry, self-consistent gas thermal balance, and stellar UV spectrum variations across A-type stars.
Archival CO isotopologue fluxes used to compute the line ratios in Figure 2 come from heterogeneous observations with potentially different uv-coverage and spatial filtering.
